# Annotations

## `Annotation`

```python
Annotation(page: Page, id: tuple[int, int], index: int)
```

A handle on one annotation of a page, as `page.annotations` lists it.

Properties read the document on every access. A handle names the
annotation's object, so it finds the annotation again after an edit
moved it; one stored as a direct dictionary in `/Annots` is found by
its position. A handle raises `StaleObjectError` while the
annotation is not on its page, and `StalePageError` while the
page is gone; it works again if undo restores them.

### `Annotation.page`

```python
Annotation.page: Page
```

The page that holds the annotation.

### `Annotation.xref`

```python
Annotation.xref: int
```

The annotation's object number, or 0 for a dictionary stored in `/Annots` itself.

### `Annotation.obj`

```python
Annotation.obj: Dictionary
```

The annotation dictionary as a live low-level handle.

### `Annotation.type`

```python
Annotation.type: AnnotationType
```

The annotation type, `AnnotationType.UNKNOWN` for a subtype pyropdf does not know.

### `Annotation.rect`

```python
Annotation.rect: Rect
```

Or set the annotation rectangle in display coordinates.

Settable.

### `Annotation.contents`

```python
Annotation.contents: str | None
```

Or set the text that the annotation shows or describes, `/Contents`.

Settable.

### `Annotation.author`

```python
Annotation.author: str | None
```

Or set the author, `/T`.

Settable.

### `Annotation.subject`

```python
Annotation.subject: str | None
```

Or set the subject, `/Subj`.

Settable.

### `Annotation.created`

```python
Annotation.created: str | None
```

The creation date as the PDF date string stored, `/CreationDate`.

### `Annotation.modified`

```python
Annotation.modified: str | None
```

The modification date as the PDF date string stored, `/M`.

### `Annotation.name`

```python
Annotation.name: str | None
```

Or set the annotation's unique name on its page, `/NM`.

Settable.

### `Annotation.icon`

```python
Annotation.icon: str | None
```

Or set the icon name of a note, stamp, or file attachment, `/Name`.

Settable.

### `Annotation.intent`

```python
Annotation.intent: str | None
```

The intent, `/IT`, such as `"FreeTextCallout"`.

### `Annotation.color`

```python
Annotation.color: Color | None
```

Or set the color of the border, title bar, or text markup, `/C`; CMYK converts to RGB.

Settable.

### `Annotation.interior_color`

```python
Annotation.interior_color: Color | None
```

Or set the fill color of a shape or line ending, `/IC`; CMYK converts to RGB.

Settable.

### `Annotation.opacity`

```python
Annotation.opacity: float
```

Or set the constant opacity, `/CA`, 1.0 when absent.

Settable.

### `Annotation.flags`

```python
Annotation.flags: AnnotationFlags
```

Or set the `/F` flags.

Settable.

### `Annotation.border`

```python
Annotation.border: Border | None
```

Or set the border that `/BS`, else `/Border`, describes, or `None` without either.

Settable.

### `Annotation.clouds`

```python
Annotation.clouds: float
```

Or set the intensity of a cloudy border, `/BE`, from 0 (none) to 2.

Squares, circles, and polygons take one; `del` and 0 remove it.

Settable.

### `Annotation.blend_mode`

```python
Annotation.blend_mode: BlendMode | None
```

Or set the blend mode that the appearance is drawn with, `/BM`, or `None` without one.

Settable.

### `Annotation.vertices`

```python
Annotation.vertices: tuple[Point, ...] | None
```

Or set the display points of a line (its two ends), polygon, or polyline.

`None` for another type or a missing or malformed geometry. Reads
refuse more than 65,536 points (`annotation_point_count`).

Settable.

### `Annotation.strokes`

```python
Annotation.strokes: tuple[tuple[Point, ...], ...] | None
```

Or set the display points of each stroke of an ink annotation, `None` for another type.

Settable.

### `Annotation.line_endings`

```python
Annotation.line_endings: tuple[LineEnding, LineEnding] | None
```

Or set the start and end shapes of a line or polyline, `None` for another type.

Settable.

### `Annotation.rotation`

```python
Annotation.rotation: int
```

Or set how far the annotation's content is turned clockwise as the page is displayed.

That is the page's rotation less the annotation's `/Rotate`, which
turns the content counterclockwise in PDF user space. Free text,
stamps, carets, and file attachments take a multiple of 90.

Settable.

### `Annotation.language`

```python
Annotation.language: str | None
```

Or set the BCP 47 language of the annotation's text, `/Lang`; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Annotation.popup_rect`

```python
Annotation.popup_rect: Rect | None
```

Or set the display rectangle of the annotation's popup, `None` without one.

Assigning a rectangle moves the popup, or adds one that the page
lists after the annotation; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Annotation.is_open`

```python
Annotation.is_open: bool
```

Or set whether the popup, or a note without one, opens when the page is shown.

Assigning needs a popup or a note.

Settable.

### `Annotation.in_reply_to`

```python
Annotation.in_reply_to: Annotation | None
```

Or set the annotation that this one replies to, `/IRT`, or `None`.

The annotation replied to belongs to the same page; a reply to an
annotation that is not listed in `page.annotations`, such as a
link, raises `StaleObjectError` on use.

Settable.

### `Annotation.replies`

```python
Annotation.replies: list[Annotation]
```

The annotations of the page that reply to this one, in `/Annots` order.

### `Annotation.pixmap`

```python
Annotation.pixmap(
    *,
    dpi: float | None = None,
    matrix: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    alpha: bool = False,
    background: tuple[int, int, int] | tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None,
    colorspace: Colorspace | Literal['gray', 'rgb'] = <Colorspace.RGB: 'rgb'>,
) -> Pixmap
```

Render the annotation's appearance alone, over its display rectangle `rect`.

The page's content and its other annotations and widgets are left
out. The appearance is the current version's, as a render draws it:
its normal appearance, or the one a render synthesizes for an
annotation without one; a hidden annotation renders as the bare
background. The options are those of `Page.pixmap`, and so
are its size limits; a rectangle that leaves no pixel of the page
raises `PdfError`, and an empty one `ValueError`. The GIL
is released while hayro renders.

### `Annotation.text`

```python
Annotation.text(
    *,
    clipped: bool = False,
    ligatures: bool = True,
    whitespace: bool = True,
    dehyphenate: bool = False,
    unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip',
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> str
```

Return the text that the annotation's appearance draws, in reading order.

The appearance is the one that `pixmap` renders, read as
`Page.text` reads a page that draws nothing else, with its
options; an appearance that draws no text, or a hidden annotation,
gives `""`. `/Contents` is not read; `contents` returns
it.

### `Annotation.sound`

```python
Annotation.sound(
    *,
    decode: bool = True,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> Sound | None
```

Return the sound that a sound annotation plays, or `None` for another kind of annotation.

`decode` and `max_size` read the `/Sound` stream as
`Stream.read` reads it, with `LimitError` code
`stream_data_size` past `max_size`. A sound annotation without a
`/Sound` stream, and a sound whose `/R`, `/C`, `/B`, `/E`,
or `/CO` is malformed, raise `MalformedPdfError`.

## `AnnotationFlags`

Annotation `/F` flags (ISO 32000-2 Table 167); the values are pymupdf's `PDF_ANNOT_IS_*`.

Members: `INVISIBLE`, `HIDDEN`, `PRINT`, `NO_ZOOM`, `NO_ROTATE`, `NO_VIEW`, `READ_ONLY`, `LOCKED`, `TOGGLE_NO_VIEW`, `LOCKED_CONTENTS`.

## `Annotations`

```python
Annotations(page: Page)
```

The annotations of a page other than links and form widgets, as `page.annotations` returns them.

The sequence lists them in `/Annots` order and reads the page on every
access; popups belong to the annotation that names them and are not
listed. `del page.annotations[i]` removes one, with its popup.

Reads reject more than 4,096 annotations or 1 MiB of annotation text per
page.

### `Annotations.__getitem__`

```python
Annotations.__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Annotation | list[Annotation]
```

Return one annotation, or a list of them for a slice.

### `Annotations.__len__`

```python
Annotations.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of annotations on the page.

### `Annotations.__iter__`

```python
Annotations.__iter__() -> Iterator[Annotation]
```

Iterate over the annotations that the page lists now.

### `Annotations.add`

```python
Annotations.add(specification: AnnotationSpecification) -> Annotation
```

Add the annotation that `specification` describes, and return it.

The annotation is drawn when its transaction commits, or before a
read in the transaction, so that every viewer draws it alike.

## `AnnotationSpecification`

`AnnotationSpecification = pyropdf.Highlight | pyropdf.Underline | pyropdf.StrikeOut | pyropdf.Squiggly | pyropdf.Note | pyropdf.Square | pyropdf.Circle | pyropdf.LineAnnotation | pyropdf.Polygon | pyropdf.PolyLine | pyropdf.Ink`

## `AnnotationType`

Annotation types by `/Subtype`; the values are pymupdf's `PDF_ANNOT_*` codes.

Members: `UNKNOWN`, `TEXT`, `LINK`, `FREE_TEXT`, `LINE`, `SQUARE`, `CIRCLE`, `POLYGON`, `POLY_LINE`, `HIGHLIGHT`, `UNDERLINE`, `SQUIGGLY`, `STRIKE_OUT`, `REDACT`, `STAMP`, `CARET`, `INK`, `POPUP`, `FILE_ATTACHMENT`, `SOUND`, `MOVIE`, `RICH_MEDIA`, `WIDGET`, `SCREEN`, `PRINTER_MARK`, `TRAP_NET`, `WATERMARK`, `THREE_D`, `PROJECTION`.

## `AttachmentIcon`

The icon of a file attachment, `/Name` (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.15).

Members: `GRAPH`, `PUSH_PIN`, `PAPERCLIP`, `TAG`.

## `Border`

```python
Border(
    width: float = 1.0,
    *,
    style: BorderStyle | None = None,
    dashes: Sequence[float] = (),
)
```

The border of an annotation: its line width, style, and dash pattern.

`dashes` lists 1 to 32 dash and gap lengths in points, which a
`BorderStyle.DASHED` border needs and no other style takes; giving
`dashes` without a style selects the dashed style. A width of 0 draws
no border.

## `BorderStyle`

The style of an annotation's border, `/BS /S` (ISO 32000-2 Table 168).

Members: `SOLID`, `DASHED`, `BEVELED`, `INSET`, `UNDERLINE`.

## `Circle`

```python
Circle(
    rect: Sequence[float],
    *,
    color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    interior_color: Color | None = None,
    border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()),
    clouds: float = 0,
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

An ellipse inscribed in a rectangle, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Square`; the ellipse and its border lie
inside `rect`.

## `Highlight`

```python
Highlight(
    rects: MarkupRects,
    *,
    color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=1.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    opacity: float = 0.4,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

A highlight over text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`rects` is one rectangle or quad, or a sequence of them, in display
coordinates, such as the result of `page.search`; a `Quad`
contributes its bounding rectangle, and one annotation holds at most
4,096. `color` fills them in multiply blending at `opacity`, and
`contents` is the text of its note. The annotation is written with its
appearance, so every viewer draws it alike.

## `Ink`

```python
Ink(
    strokes: Iterable[Iterable[Point | Sequence[float]]],
    *,
    color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()),
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

Freehand strokes, each through one or more display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`color` draws every stroke with round caps and joins at the `border`
width; one annotation holds at most 65,536 points in all.

## `LineAnnotation`

```python
LineAnnotation(
    start: Point | Sequence[float],
    end: Point | Sequence[float],
    *,
    color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    interior_color: Color | None = None,
    border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()),
    line_endings: tuple[LineEnding, LineEnding] = (<LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>, <LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>),
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

A straight line between two display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`color` strokes the line with the `border` width and dashes, and
`line_endings` gives the shapes at its start and end, whose closed
shapes `interior_color` fills. The annotation's rectangle is the line's
bounds, widened for the stroke and the endings.

## `LineEnding`

The shape at an end of a line or polyline, `/LE` (ISO 32000-2 Table 179).

Closed shapes are filled with the annotation's interior color.

Members: `NONE`, `SQUARE`, `CIRCLE`, `DIAMOND`, `OPEN_ARROW`, `CLOSED_ARROW`, `BUTT`, `REVERSED_OPEN_ARROW`, `REVERSED_CLOSED_ARROW`, `SLASH`.

## `MarkupRects`

`MarkupRects = collections.abc.Sequence[float] | pyropdf.Quad | collections.abc.Iterable[collections.abc.Sequence[float] | pyropdf.Quad]`

## `Note`

```python
Note(
    at: Point | Sequence[float],
    *,
    contents: str | None = None,
    icon: NoteIcon = <NoteIcon.NOTE: 'note'>,
    color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=1.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    is_open: bool = False,
)
```

A note shown as an icon, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`at` is the display point of the icon's top-left corner; the icon is
20 points square, and its flags ask viewers to keep it upright on a
turned page. `contents` is the note's text, `icon` its picture,
`color` the icon's fill, and `is_open` whether a viewer opens the
note when it shows the page. Add a popup by assigning
`Annotation.popup_rect`.

## `NoteIcon`

The icon of a note, `/Name` (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.4).

Members: `COMMENT`, `HELP`, `INSERT`, `KEY`, `NEW_PARAGRAPH`, `NOTE`, `PARAGRAPH`.

## `Polygon`

```python
Polygon(
    vertices: Iterable[Point | Sequence[float]],
    *,
    color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    interior_color: Color | None = None,
    border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()),
    clouds: float = 0,
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

A closed polygon through two or more display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`color` strokes the outline and `interior_color` fills it; `clouds`
from 0 to 2 draws the outline as a cloud whose bumps grow with it. One
annotation holds at most 65,536 points.

## `PolyLine`

```python
PolyLine(
    vertices: Iterable[Point | Sequence[float]],
    *,
    color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    interior_color: Color | None = None,
    border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()),
    line_endings: tuple[LineEnding, LineEnding] = (<LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>, <LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>),
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

An open line through two or more display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `LineAnnotation`, with `line_endings` at
the first and last points; one annotation holds at most 65,536 points.

## `Sound`

```python
Sound(
    data: bytes,
    rate: float,
    channels: int,
    bits: int,
    encoding: SoundEncoding,
    compression: str | None,
)
```

The sound of a sound annotation, `/Sound`, as `Annotation.sound` reads it.

`data` holds the samples as the stream stores them after its filters,
or the stream's bytes before them when read with `decode=False`; the
samples stay in `encoding` and, for a compressed sound, in the format
that `compression` names.

## `SoundEncoding`

How a sound's samples encode amplitudes, `/E` (ISO 32000-2 Table 208).

Members: `RAW`, `SIGNED`, `MU_LAW`, `A_LAW`.

## `Square`

```python
Square(
    rect: Sequence[float],
    *,
    color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    interior_color: Color | None = None,
    border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()),
    clouds: float = 0,
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

A rectangle, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`rect` is in display coordinates. `color` strokes the border and
`interior_color` fills the inside; either may be `None`. The border
lies inside `rect`, and `clouds` from 0 to 2 draws it as a cloud
whose bumps grow with it, inside `rect` too. `opacity` and
`blend_mode` apply to both paints, and `contents` is the text of the
annotation's note.

## `Squiggly`

```python
Squiggly(
    rects: MarkupRects,
    *,
    color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

A wavy line under text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Highlight`; `color` draws a zigzag
two points wide along the bottom of each rectangle, at most 65,536 points
in all (`annotation_point_count`).

## `StampIcon`

The stamps of ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.12, `/Name`; pymupdf's `STAMP_*` codes in their order.

Members: `APPROVED`, `AS_IS`, `CONFIDENTIAL`, `DEPARTMENTAL`, `EXPERIMENTAL`, `EXPIRED`, `FINAL`, `FOR_COMMENT`, `FOR_PUBLIC_RELEASE`, `NOT_APPROVED`, `NOT_FOR_PUBLIC_RELEASE`, `SOLD`, `TOP_SECRET`, `DRAFT`.

## `StrikeOut`

```python
StrikeOut(
    rects: MarkupRects,
    *,
    color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0),
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

A line through text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Highlight`; `color` draws a one-point
line through the middle of each rectangle.

## `Underline`

```python
Underline(
    rects: MarkupRects,
    *,
    color: Color = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=1.0, alpha=1.0),
    opacity: float = 1.0,
    contents: str | None = None,
)
```

A line under text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Highlight`; `color` draws a one-point
line just above the bottom edge of each rectangle.
